industry.beds: India has far fewer hospital beds than the WHO's 3 per 1,000 people in Max's states: Delhi 2.2 (0.8 private), Haryana 1.4 (0.9 private), Maharashtra 1.8 (1.6), Uttar Pradesh 1.3 (1.0) (CRISIL, via Max's deck). Health-insurance premiums grew 18% a year from FY18 to FY25, and group plus individual policies now cover 58% of insured lives (35% in FY18).
industry.metros: Metro hospitals bill more per day: on Max's comparison for Q1FY27, ARPOB was ₹82k at Max (73% of beds in metros), ₹74k at Fortis (74%), ₹70k at Medanta (50%), ₹67k at Apollo (58%), ₹53k at Narayana (68%) and ₹47k at KIMS (51%).
themes: Insurance & corporates rose to 37.8% of Max's revenue in Q1FY27 (35.8% a year earlier); ~6% automatic price revision with insurers from Sep-Oct 2026

CGHS capped margins on high-value drugs (MoU, Oct-2025): oncology fell from 26% to 21-22% of Max's IP revenue; a CGHS rate revision (~₹140 cr a year) partly offsets. Max is cutting institutional share (20.9%)

On 30-Sep-2026 the Supreme Court called markups of up to 10x on cancer drugs 'carnage' and asked the government to look at a uniform 16% trade margin; hospital stocks fell ~5% that day. Pharmacy margins are a material part of hospital profits

Listed chains plan large additions (Antique: sector beds +54% over FY26-30E); Max itself plans ~4,000 beds in 3-4 years. More supply in NCR raises doctor costs (Max's clinician costs +230bp YoY in Q4FY26)
India had ~7.3 lakh medical tourists in 2024 (Ministry of Tourism/CRISIL); Max's international revenue ₹897 cr in FY26 (+20%), ~9% of hospital revenue
A Parliamentary Standing Committee report (Aug-2026) discussed affordability and FDI caps; the NMC draft lets for-profit companies run medical colleges

street.consensusNote: Every dated note we found from Jun-Sep 2026 values Max on EV/EBITDA (Network EBITDA, FY28E or 12-month forward; three use SOTP with the hospital business at 30-33x). Post-Q1 targets: ₹1,150-1,410 (average ₹1,264 for the four houses). Only Antique (Hold) is not a Buy. Brokers' EPS (₹19.0 FY27E, ₹23.6-23.7 FY28E) is Network PAT ÷ shares, ~10-15% above consolidated EPS.
street.methodNote: Street EV/EBITDA is on Network EBITDA (includes the three PHF societies, ~₹290 cr of FY26 EBITDA) and Network net debt (excludes lease liabilities, ~₹590 cr). Our model is on MHIL consolidated numbers (Screener), so we translate: PL's 30x FY28E Network EBITDA is ~35x our FY28E consolidated EBITDA (see Valuation).

moat: Location and land
Strong
~73% of beds in metros; 2,548 operational beds in Delhi NCR at 79% occupancy; land banks in Saket, Gurugram, Noida, Lucknow, Mohali, Pune for ~4,300 more beds
Brownfield beds next to full hospitals are the cheapest, fastest growth in the industry
Clinical depth and brand
Strong
~4,700 liver, ~6,000 kidney and ~2,300 bone-marrow transplants to date; oncology ~22% of IP revenue; JCI-accredited hubs (Saket, BLK, Nanavati)
Supports the highest ARPOB in the listed sector (₹81.9k)
Operating efficiency
Strong
Network occupancy ~75% for 4+ years even while adding beds; EBITDA per bed ₹71-74 lakh vs ₹47-58 lakh at Medanta, Apollo, Fortis (company comparison)
Turnaround track record (Lucknow EBITDA ~5x its acquisition level, per CMD)
Payor mix
Mixed
Institutional (CGHS/ECHS/PSU) still ~21% of revenue and 32% of beds; management calls it loss-making; insurance 38%, self-pay 33%, international 9%
Improving, but government price actions can hit Max harder than peers (as oncology showed)
Scale vs Apollo
Neutral
Second-largest listed chain; Apollo has ~2x the revenue and a pharmacy/digital ecosystem
No pricing power over insurers beyond what location gives
Doctors
Watch
Clinician costs +230bp YoY in Q4FY26 as Max pre-hired for new capacity and competition for senior doctors in NCR rose
Doctor retention is the real moat and the main cost risk
Structure
Watch
Three PHF societies (Saket East, Smart, Patparganj) are run by Max but not owned; ~₹746 cr lent to one of them
Economic interest is through contracts lasting to 2064-2105, not ownership
critiques: Returns are falling: company pre-tax ROCE 25.9% (FY25) → 21.8% (FY26), and ~₹7,000 cr of project capex to FY30 keeps them down for years
Growth slowed to 10-12% (network) in H2FY26 as CGHS drug caps cut oncology; Q1FY27 +16% needed acquisitions and new towers
Q3/Q4FY26 calls; analysts (Citi, BofA) on the Q1 call
Street EPS is on Network PAT (includes PHF societies Max does not own); consolidated EPS is 10-15% lower
Pharmacy and drug margins face regulatory risk (CGHS caps, Supreme Court remarks on 30-Sep-2026)
Choice Equity Broking via Reuters/ThePrint; Q4FY26 call
Working capital worsened: DSO 95 days, free-cash conversion 56% in Q1FY27 (62-65% normal)
Pay: the CMD earned ₹27.4 cr fixed in FY26, 627x the median employee
Even after a 28% fall from the Jul-2025 high, Max trades at ~29x our FY28E consolidated EV/EBITDA, the most expensive large hospital stock after Aster and KIMS
gaps: Mature vs new hospital split (beds, occupancy, ARPOB, margins) is not disclosed; the company gives a pre-tax ROCE of ~29-31% for units over four years old (excl. CWIP) vs 21-22% overall, and EBITDA per bed for the network only.
Region-level revenue was dropped from the Q1FY27 earnings deck (shown only in the 17-Aug-2026 investor deck); hospital-level EBITDA is not disclosed.

Capex per bed: no project-by-project cost except Vaishali (₹425 cr for 202 beds, ~₹2.1 cr/bed incl. structure) and Shaheed Path (~₹1,400 cr for 712 beds, ~₹2.0 cr/bed). The deck's ₹6,961 cr FY27-30 outflow excludes land, routine capex and unfirmed projects; the split between Max's own capex and loans to PHFs is not given.
Routine (maintenance) capex is not disclosed separately; we assume ₹200-240 cr a year.

Lease liabilities that asset-light built-to-suit hospitals (Zirakpur, Dehradun, Thane, Pitampura) will add are not disclosed; we estimate from the Dwarka precedent (+₹372 cr of lease liabilities in FY25 for ~300 beds).
Acquisition prices for Lucknow, Nagpur and Noida (FY25) are not in the files we read; Kalinga ~₹298 cr is disclosed; YPPL's price is not.
Average operational beds by year are not disclosed; we derive them from revenue, ARPOB and occupancy (OBDs ÷ 365 ÷ occupancy).
Max Lab gross revenue (as used in the ARPOB definition) is not disclosed; we use net revenue (₹201 cr FY26), a small difference.

conflicts: Q1FY27 PAT: the press release's Network PAT is ₹357 cr (after OCI); consolidated PAT on Screener is ₹323 cr; some media quoted ₹320-323 cr. We use consolidated in the model and Network for KPIs.
Vaishali tower timing: the 17-Aug-2026 deck chart places it in FY29; the 13-Aug-2026 release says commissioning in Q4FY30. We use FY30.
Shaheed Path, Lucknow: 712 beds for ~₹1,400 cr (May-2026 release) vs 400 beds in the FY30 column of the Aug-2026 deck (312 more shown as later potential). We use 400 in FY30.
Antique's rating: Business Today (29-Jun-2026) reports HOLD at ₹1,170; one search summary called it Buy. We use the article.
ARPOB peers: the deck's p.9 (Medanta ₹70k, Apollo ₹67k) and p.11 (different bases and periods) differ; we quote p.9 for Q1FY27.
